free_tier.stated: There is no free tier: disposable screens run on prepaid credit from $10, and $5 of credit for disposable screens is granted when a card is added, about 140 hours. A persistent screen is $20 a month at the founding price, or $0.035 an hour while a disposable screen runs.
free_tier.notes: The $5 of credit for disposable screens is conditional on adding a card; the pricing page calls it a trial credit and says it is about 140 hours. The persistent price of $20 a screen a month is a founding price, kept while the subscriber stays, against a $25 list price; yearly is $200 for 12 months. Each screen is 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and 50 GB disk.

per_object_cap.stated: file upload or download is capped at 64 MiB; a screen has a 50 GB disk; templates are 5 per organization and snapshots 3 per screen, up to 50 GB of changes
per_object_cap.notes: The 64 MiB figure is the single file transfer cap. The 50 GB figure is the screen's disk, not a per-object limit.

retention.stated: every call on a screen is kept in its history for 30 days; a stopped disposable screen is deleted after 7 days; recovery copies of screen disks are kept 7 nights and are not a backup service

egress.terms: exports and switching are free, including their data transfer, and a screen's whole disk can be exported at any time as one qcow2 image convertible to raw or VMDK; outbound traffic for a screen goes through the user's own proxy and fails closed when that proxy is down, while inbound connections are refused and ports expose only HTTP and WebSocket behind a token or secret link

interface_detail: A screen is driven through a REST API with plain HTTP and JSON and a Bearer API key, a TypeScript SDK, a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.trykubi.com, and a dashboard with live view and Take control. Ports give a service inside a screen its own HTTPS URL on trykubi.dev behind a token or link.
tooling: npm install @trykubi/sdk, curl against the REST API, or an MCP connection from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor or VS Code; a Python SDK generated from the same spec comes later. Files move through the API, the SDK or exec, up to 64 MiB each.
chaining: A persistent Linux desktop with browser logins and root access gives a computer-use agent a stable address, while the user's own proxy carries all screen traffic and an exported qcow2 disk moves the work to another provider.

limits.value: $20 a screen a month at the founding price, or $200 a year for 12 months; $0.035 an hour while a disposable screen runs, from prepaid credit of $10 to $500
60 requests a minute per key for each screen, at least 300; 2 screenshots a second per screen; 10 other calls a second per screen; 300 requests a second through ports, bursting to 2,000
64 MiB per file upload or download; 3 open ports per screen included in the price

limits_note: Each organization has one screen cap across persistent and disposable screens, so a runaway agent cannot exceed it; creating one past the cap gives 402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Disposable screens stop when credit runs out, persistent screens never do. Screens have no public inbound connection; ports carry HTTP and WebSocket only, not raw TCP. There is no GPU and no Windows or macOS.
binding_note: The prepaid credit and flat monthly screen price are the first constraint: disposable screens stop when the credit is spent and persistent screens bill monthly whether running or stopped, before the per-key request rate or 64 MiB file cap is reached.

identity_cost.detail: The terms say 'Anyone can sign up and start using Kubi at once' and '3.3 You sign in with a link sent to your email, with GitHub or Google, or with a passkey'; section 3.4 adds that the provider may ask the user to verify identity or payment method. A card is needed for the $5 trial credit and to buy a persistent screen through Stripe. No phone number, ID document or institution is stated as a sign-up requirement. The user must be at least 18 and the service is for business use only.

reliability_note: Kubi promises no uptime; screens are credited for a fault over 4 hours if claimed within 30 days, and the agreement disclaims that websites will accept traffic from screen IP addresses. A card that declines or needs 3-D Secure fails a screen create with PAYMENT_REQUIRED; a port request over its limit gets 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After.
confidence_note: The $20 founding price, $0.035 hourly rate, $10 minimum top-up, no-free-tier statement, $5 card credit, 4 vCPU/8 GB/50 GB shape and free disk export are quoted from Kubi's own pricing page read on 2026-11-24; the sign-in methods, free data-transfer export and 30-day history are quoted from its terms; the 64 MiB and request-rate figures are quoted from its limits reference.
